- Overestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially < 0.25) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for such periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially > 0.6) — increase forecast by 2–5% for such periods.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price peaks — cap forecast growth at 3–5% above prior peak unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show upward trend, reduce forecast slope slightly; if downward, increase slightly.
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment is volatile (±0.35 in 3-day window), add 1–2% smoothing penalty to avoid overreaction.
- Lag correction: if true outcome is 2–3 days below forecast, adjust next forecast down by 1–2% to avoid over-leverage on momentum.
